notes: §1985:XIII.3.19.4 GR2: the RWCS 'adds into the sum counter the value in each data item referenced by identifier-1. This addition is consistent with the rules for arithmetic statements' (no SIZE ERROR phrase, so a size error leaves the result undefined, §1985:VI.6.4.2). EmitReportConstruction registers each term (SumAddition, AddSumTerm), GenerateCore subtotals after control-break processing through Accumulate, and BindRolledValues supplies crossfoot addends. Probes at 85 (v1, u1, v2, witness 06): decimal alignment with truncation (1.005 into V99 gives 2.00), signed addends into S9 (-9) and into unsigned 99 (09), 18-digit addends (-999999999999999999), a subscripted addend whose subscript changes between GENERATEs (5+7-9 = 03+), an OCCURS DEPENDING ON element, the same addend written twice (18), a same-group crossfoot (9); on overflow the counter is left unchanged, one of the undefined results. Missing part: the 2002 SUM forms are not refused at --std 85, so an arithmetic-expression addend (SUM WS-A + 1, v5: 13), SUM OF and ROUNDED compile and are added. kb/Work PB5242 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-pipe/slice-51.json).

next.reason: Both add the value of each addend into the sum counter by arithmetic-statement rules (§2023:13.18.54.4 GR6 'the value added is that of the corresponding sum counter' for a sum-counter operand; §2023:13.18.54.4 GR9 multiple addends summed separately). The size-error result differs: 1985 says only 'This addition is consistent with the rules for arithmetic statements', i.e. an addition with no SIZE ERROR phrase, where per §1985:VI.6.4.2 'the values of the affected resultant identifiers are undefined'. §2023:13.18.54.4 GR3 makes it 'consistent with the general rules of the ADD statement with the ON SIZE ERROR phrase' and 'Each addition is tested for size error; if a size error occurs, the EC-REPORT-SUM-SIZE exception condition is set to exist' (sum counter left unchanged, size error indicator set). An undefined run-time result became a defined one; no compile-time refusal is involved.
